issues.description: The problem statement and the template (Main.java) expect a Farm class with a no-argument constructor (students are instructed to "Initialize the ArrayList in a constructor with no arguments" and Main instantiates Farm with new Farm()). The solution's Farm implementation only provides a constructor Farm(int initialCapacity). This constructor-parameter mismatch contradicts the specification and the template usage and will confuse or block students who follow the instructions or try to compile the provided Main code.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a no-argument constructor in Farm (e.g. public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); }) to match the problem statement and template usage, or update the problem statement and template to explicitly require and use Farm(int initialCapacity). The preferred fix is to add the no-arg constructor so students can instantiate Farm with new Farm() as instructed.
